## Details

### elekloader

Mod loader: user supplies the stock OS file, the tool builds the custom .syx locally. Device table in the README (3016dca, 2026-11-08): Digitakt mk1 and Digitone mk1/Keys supported; Digitakt II 1.17 and Digitone II 1.12 experimental; Octatrack 1.40C supported (linkable core boots on an MKII); Model:Cycles and Model:Samples 1.13 supported (builds work on both units); Analog Rytm MKII 1.74 supported; Analog Four MKII 1.56 experimental proof of concept (hook bus, mod storage, unused DDR and recovery checked on a unit). Canonical repo is unclear: the forum post also embeds github.com/elekloader/elekloader (web app at elekloader.github.io/elekloader); forks exist (AvroraPolnareff, naturarum, toonst, simonjohansson); none is listed, as none has changes of its own. Forum: builder issue reported 2026-10-19. Licence GPL-2.0-or-later. 2026-11-10 (8daa2ea): the shop's list, forms and bots moved to elekloader/shop (#338); mods are submitted there. machine-pages 1.8-1.10, machines-dn1 0.5/0.6 and machines-dn2 0.5 add mono machines and MIDI CCs (emulator-tested per TESTS.md). The linker now refuses odd jump targets into mod RAM after a Digitakt II froze at boot (I61). The README offers a Windows .exe; not every release carries the macOS .dmg. 2026-11-10 (main): core-ar2 0.13 opens the Rytm MKII's TEST slots 44-52 to mod machines, adds per-voice trig and velocity getters, screen calls through stock's routines and per-mod knob ids; machine-pages 1.7 tagged. 2026-11-12 (main): core-a4mk2 0.6 brings core-ar2 0.10-0.13's foundations to the Analog Four MKII (field defaults, the modified mark, the project-save event, payloads, knob looks, screen calls) and a 37.7 MB mods' area. Builds pick older core or helper versions by themselves when a mod patches a place a newer one took (Tone+FX's Digitakt files and Digi EQ 1.0c link with DT1 core 4.0 only; OB-1 0.6 with machine-pages 1.2), and released versions stay available while a listed mod needs them. 2026-11-13 (main): a third file family, ELE2, for the Analog Rytm MKI OS 1.74 (Modwerk's Rytm MKI research holds the measurements behind the profile); the README's table also names 1.73, the profile only 1.74. core-ot 0.9-0.40 opens about 40 more Octatrack events and tables to mods (mutes, sequencer moments, LFO waves, popup rows, PATTERN SETTINGS and PERSONALIZE rows, the playback increment, card file calls, the engine task's jobs, a block to DSP core 1). 2026-11-15 (FORMAT, SDK, CORES): std1 'standard events': a mod that sets events std1 subscribes to device- neutral event names, each core maps them to its own tables, and a subscription the core does not map is refused at link time; std1 and native mods link in one build. core-a4mk2 0.7 is the first core with it and adds native A4 events for knob turns, the analog voice frame and modulation edits. A frame-check build that copied one voice's analog frame words over another's silenced track 1 and was fixed in 0.3 (unit or emulator not stated). 2026-11-16 (docs/CORES.md, DRIVE.md, FORMAT.md, core-dn1 README): on the Digitone mk1 the build descriptor now carries the stock bytes of each flashed range (ABI 1.2), and TELOS's linker refuses a +Drive mod site that is not stock on the unit, overlaps the flashed build or another mod, or a region outside a free area (link codes 21-28). core-dn1 5.4's core_stock_info copies the OS image to 0x44200000 before the OS runs. 2026-11-17 (ADAPTING, FORMAT, core-ot, settings-ot, dspload-ot, core-a4mk2 READMEs): core-ot 0.41/0.42 add 16 Octatrack events (tempo, scenes, card mount and USB DISK MODE, previews, recorder commands, pages, track select, windows, crossfader, pattern select and edits, arrangement); new dspload-ot 0.2 sends DSP code at run time (mod.json `dsp_load`), also for TELOS card mods; refusal code 23 `early` for a site the OS ran before the +Drive or card link. On the Analog Four MKII the lock service is now checked on a unit. 2026-11-18 (v0.11.0, docs/DRIVE.md, CORES.md, drive-loader-a4mk2 and drive-loader-ar2 READMEs): v0.11.0 ships the newest core of every device, core-a4mk2 0.9 included. The Analog Four MKII gets its own +Drive mods loader (drive-loader-a4mk2 0.1, not yet run): stock 1.56 keeps the +Drive as raw sectors with no file system, so the loader keeps its own two-copy store in sectors stock never addresses. The Rytm loader (0.6) now reads each file into the +Drive area itself (a 64 KB floor replaces the 512 KB staging buffer), and +Drive mods may hold storage fields, sites over the OS, claims, tables of their own, knob ids and std1 subscriptions where the build's descriptor flags allow (descriptor ABI 1.3). drive-loader-ar2's README asks for core-ar2 0.14 while core-ar2's mod.json at the tag reads 0.13. New A4 MKII check mods for live recording, the sequencer and moments (read as expected in the emulator, 2026-11-14). 2026-11-20 (ADAPTING, CORES, DRIVE, FORMAT; core-ar2 README and SKIPS.md; core-dt2, core-dn2, core-a4mk2, drive-loader, smpl-machines READMEs; new AR2 and DT2 examples): core-dt2 1.1 keeps mods' project and kit data in bytes stock writes as zeros (191 bytes a kit), adds value rows, a per-frame parameter event and key LEDs; core-dt2 1.2 and core-dn2 0.5 add what TELOS needs on the unit (card ready, project save and load, crash, restart, task list), checked in digikit's emulator only, not yet on a unit. core-ar2 0.15: knob faces, mod folders in the +Drive sample browser, pad strikes before stock and LED colours, a held USB input gain step, note ends, track mutes, DIN MIDI out, machines given slots by count; 0.16: four optional CPU skips, off at boot (silent voices, idle sample layer, the UI's dynamic_cast, idle delay and reverb), two of which change the sound slightly, and GLOBAL submenus. The linker hands out machine slots, page ids and mod-declared id pools by count, kept in the lockfile. New smpl-machines (a SMPL page machine layer) and smpl-knob-c. Five new Rytm check examples and kit-memo-dt2. core-a4mk2 0.10's core_project_keep lets the A4 loader's APPLY & RESTART keep unsaved project changes. core-a4mk2's README now says core 0.2's pages drew identically on a unit (OS 1.56).

_Latest seen (2026-10-31, secondary directories): altstrument.org and the repo (read 2026-10-31): canonical repo is github.com/elekloader/elekloader (183 commits, 103 stars, GPL-2.0-or-later); web app moved to elekloader.github.io/elekloader; the Mac app was absent from v0.9.0 because signing secrets need renewing. v0.9.0 cores: core-4.1 and core-4.1-os1.54 (Digitakt mk1), core-dn1-4.1.1 and -os1.44 (Digitone mk1), core-ar2-0.8 (Analog Rytm MKII 1.74), core-ot-0.8 (Octatrack 1.40C), core-mc-0.3 (Model:Cycles), core-ms-0.1 (Model:Samples), core-a4 0.1-0.4 (Analog Four MKII 1.56). Kit 0.7.0 catalog: 19 cores, 88 mods. machine-pages 1.2/1.3/1.5 need core 3.0+ on Digitakt mk1 and refuse NEIGHBOR 0.6, SOPHIE 1.1.13 and digichain-based machine mods beside them; fxkit 0.1 gives Digitone effect mods a shared mixer, two LFOs, pattern p-locks and a CPU guard; core-dn1 4.1 adds ev_note_queue; kit 0.6.0 gives 4.0 cores larger RAM areas (256 KB Digitakt, 1.25 MB Digitone). docs/ includes AGENTS.md, DEVICES.md, MACHINES-DN2, SHARC-DN2, CORES, FORMAT, BUILDING, ADAPTING (not all read yet - see hardware/MINING.md). The earlier irpina/elekloader repo is where the author's older releases lived._

_Related: uses tool `digikit` (README: checks or gates run in digikit's emulator (not shipped)) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

### Modwerk (formerly Octamod)

2026-11-12: the Octatrack card firmware builder is retired: modules reach an Octatrack only through the Modwerk base, over USB or as one set file (MODWERK0.SET) on the card; Tuner, Stem Rec and Temp Save paused until they have base versions; Spectrum, Modulation, Character and MIDI Scenes removed for good; CPU-rendered machines get a budget (CPU FULL) after FM Synth froze an MKII (I79); POLY8 and FM Synth carry a Heavy CPU badge; checks refuse writes into the stock DELAY table and odd jump targets; the DT2 base hides the raw +Drive block write from modules; Octatrack modules moved to sdk/octatrack/modules; new experimental Crossfader and Live Looper for the Digitakt I (OS 1.54) and Amiga, a tracker-style sample machine, for the Octatrack. 2026-11-11/12: the Octatrack base and USB installs are open to everyone (first install still from the card, at most 20 modules per set, 24 since 2026-11-14; Tuner, Stem Rec and Temp Save card-only); USB Audio is off unless the set has the USB Audio module; skipping modules at boot moved from FUNC to holding PROJ at power-on (MKI keeps FUNC); the octabam pin is frozen (Modwerk follows only elekloader upstream); Analog BD 0.1.7 has a new 909 model; base-update and SYNTIZ incidents I75 and I76. 2026-11-09/10: Octatrack beta: the silence after USB DISK MODE (finding 72) was the base mistaking stock's DSP pause for a stall, fixed (I69); FM Synth with many FLEX tracks no longer loses the audio on PLAY; the Octatrack page asks for a power cycle when the DSP has stopped; Temp Save 0.1.0 withdrawn from USB installs (card build stays). Modwerk also loads effects onto Zoom MultiStomp pedals now (ZDL files over USB; not an Elektron device). Browser-based hub, builds locally from the user's own stock OS. Browse mods by device, forum with a section per device, shared SDK. Dubspot (13 Oct): several modules are still early prototypes. last_activity = date of the Dubspot article, not a forum post. 2026-11-02: three Analog Rytm MKII modules by npp1993 moved into the library (Pipo Loop 0.1.1, Sample RATE 0.1.0, Silent Pad+Trig Settings 0.6.0, all experimental, OS 1.74; linkable together with core-ar2 0.7, Filter Hz and Loop Sync; the packages themselves not yet run on a unit). `_submissions/` takes no new modules. The Octatrack USB beta also works on the MKI. 2026-11-03: the site now lets you download a built Analog Rytm MKII .syx (after confirming you know how to get back to stock); new Rytm module quick-velocity-aftertouch-assign with a verification note. Zoom pedals: an effect whose group+ID clashes with one already on the pedal is moved to a free local Delay ID 958-1023 (ID only in the ZDL header at 0x40-0x41, no checksum); two effects with the same group and ID froze an MS-70CDR at boot until its ROM was reprogrammed. 2026-11-04/05: Rytm MKII downloads on (records); npp1993's Control In Actions (footswitch or 0-5 V gate on EXP/CV IN as ACTION for MUTE and more) and Quick Velocity+Aftertouch Assign join the library, Silent Pad+Trig Settings 0.7.0; euclidean 1.1.6 for Digitakt I 1.53/1.54 reported working on a unit by sumedho (all cases, save/reload, power cycle). 2026-11-08 to 11-10 (74c9eb2): Rytm library gains comp-preview, kit-ab, lfo-rnd and voice-dac (from rytm2_mods, unit runs on the Modwerk base), ctrl-in-perf and scene-mutes (from rytm-mods-src 0017/0018, unit runs T208/T210/T221), Improved Machine Browser and MIDI Mute; the Octatrack key bus moved to the tail of the first FX2 slot (checked on an MKI and an MKII); a Digitakt II audio scheduler is proposed (emulator only); Zoom MS-70CDR pedal work (out of scope here). 2026-11-12/13: Octatrack base: a stall record now keeps the 128 frames before it; an installed Sidechain no longer causes NO ROOM on every pick after a restart (I96); a new USB device revision (bcdDevice 0x0101) repairs Windows hosts that could not open the unit (I100); a machine engine's DSP price moved into its package; the base refuses a module machine or effect pick while the CPU meter is at 85 % or more; VECTOR 0.3.2 fixes a whole-bank reset (I95); SYNTIZ and Tape Echo get a Heavy CPU badge. Rytm MKII: the send-bus base gains digital voices; new Improved AMP and BD ANALOG (I97-I99). module:doctor covers Digitakt II modules; a Digitakt II pre-send render hook is proposed (emulator only). FRACT, an Octatrack granular machine draft by ex1010, has a functional unit report (2026-11-10). 2026-11-14 (second pass): the Digitakt II moved from research to preview: the site builds core 1.0 with library modules in the browser, downloads stay off, OS 1.17 only; the first DT2 library module is Track Names; DT2 phrase modules can continue phrases across empty steps, follow microtimed trigs and save settings in a project archive. Octatrack: a two-step base update for units whose RAM stage is too small; the CPU guard counts the picked machine's price and judges a stopped unit by its last playing load (I105); POLY8 0.3.3 and FM Synth 0.1.3 cost far less while installed on no track (FM Synth 0.1.3 also fixes track 1's LFO 3); `device:price` measures a module's cost; a new Octatrack Diagnostics page on the site. 2026-11-14 (changelog, verification): an Octatrack module set may hold 24 modules (was 20, still temporary); the base may grow to 1.5 MiB, so units on a base older than 2026-11-13 take it as two USB updates, and a base update retries up to four times when a reply goes missing before the write starts. New project and bank events (load, save, reload, new project, Part save and clear) let a module keep its own file beside the project. Amiga 0.3.0 (experimental) adds a SYNC stretch mode that follows the project tempo; in a RAM trial on an MKII an earlier build of it restarted after about 90 s on a twin that also carried a base change under test (I109). Filter Hz 1.2.1 (Rytm MKII, from rytm2_mods' port of 0008-filter-hz) widens the box behind a locked FRQ so kHz values fit; a maintainer ran it on a Rytm MKII on OS 1.74 on 2026-11-14. 2026-11-16 (changelog 2026-11-14/15, LINK.md, TEST_RUNNER.md): Rytm MKII development bases carry a SysEx USB link (screen, memory, keys, encoders, remote flash, and a boot from RAM with no flash write), and a test runner plays scripted cases on rytm-emu or a unit over it. Filter Hz 1.3.0 shows the FX track's delay and reverb HPF, LPF and reverb FRQ in Hz. 2026-11-17 (changelog 2026-11-16/17, verification, module docs): Octatrack base versions start at 0.7 (shown as MODWERK BASE 0.7 on the unit; 0.7.1 to 0.7.5 the same day): PROJ > MODWERK > MODULES switches installed modules on and off; a project remembers which machine each track uses, so a missing machine is named instead of playing FLEX; one module may use 288 KiB (was 128) and may borrow sample memory while installed; windowed modules such as Tuner can come over USB (base 0.7.5); packages are no longer refused for sharing byte runs with stock; every Octatrack module must name its CPU price (`resources.cpuPrice`); `module:doctor` reports DSP register writes against each hook site's contract; stall records name each DSP core's last packet. New Octatrack modules Kits and MIDI Scenes 0.3.0 (experimental ports of octabam's modules, short RAM trials on the owner's MKII); the Octakit draft is removed. New Digitakt I module CC Remap. Rytm MKII: a third base variant, voices; Ping Pong Loop folded into Improved SMPL 0.6.x; size-only updates of several modules run on the author's unit; Analog Rytm MKI builds are refused when the update exceeds the upgrade buffer or touches the boot-flash writers. Goal pages for contributors on the Digitakt II and the Syntakt (no Syntakt module yet). Field diagnostics 12-16 Nov: 87 units. A dialog on the site says the project's future is uncertain and asks for maintainers. 2026-11-18 (changelog 2026-11-07..17, verification, machine guides): Octatrack base 0.7.7 skips stock's delay work for tracks whose delay is silent (CPU meter 41 to 34 % with DELAY on every track); a machine's CPU price is now its mean cost per playing track (FM Synth 0.1.4: 6 %, seven tracks a Part); DSP voices book only what the bank's Parts use (core 0 up to 3,120 cycles); a shared scale file for Octatrack modules. Rytm MKII: sets linked by Modwerk's own linker may use 704 KiB or 3.7 MiB of DDR above the 128 KiB mod area; the voices base drops the FX lock words (1,752 B more for modules). Rytm MKI SDK guide published (research). Digitakt II: the site builds Modwerk's base 8650bb8a on core-dt2 1.1 (elekloader#221 at 0df8409), downloads still off; new modules MIDI Engine (Rytm), Euclidean Scale and Mute Latch (DT2), Vibrato (Octatrack, from octabam). Machine maintainers may now merge a machine's first module releases; pull requests that change a built package stay drafts until that build ran on a unit. The dialog saying the project's future is uncertain was removed. 2026-11-18, later (changelog, OCTATRACK_PACKAGE_DSP_HOOKS): Octatrack base 0.7.8 makes the per-track sound-source hook (DSP site 5) a chain (#1098): the base offers each track to every installed DSP track machine in turn and the first that owns it plays it, so a second DSP machine (BlackPyramids) can install over USB beside Analog BD; Analog BD's package and sound are unchanged. The key bus (option B) is merged (#737). 2026-11-19 (changelog 2026-11-14..19, DESKTOP_APP, MACHINE_RECIPE, HOOKS, MODULE_PERFORMANCE, arr-rows, butter- fingers, Digitone II verification): every contribution, core work included, now comes to Modwerk as a pull request, and every machine is to get a Modwerk base (Digitone II and Analog Four MKII included). Octatrack base 0.7.8 lets modules rest when unused; 0.7.9 adds a shared Part Edit menu and fixes an effect lost after a project load (I154). A desktop app (Electron, WebUSB and Web MIDI) is in development, Windows only so far, never run against a unit. Digitone II: core-dn2 0.3 builds booted on a second unit from Transfer, and stock 1.12 came back with a normal update; no Modwerk module can be built for it yet. Two stock Octatrack arrangement bugs found by Arr Rows (SB33, SB34). 2026-11-20 (changelog 2026-11-18/19, verification 2026-11-19 beta diagnostics, OCTATRACK_DRIVING, MODULE_PERFORMANCE, machines guide, micro-timing README/TESTING, Digitone II GOAL): most of the day's changelog is web app, agent board and tooling. Octatrack: base 0.7.9 is the site's base since 2026-11-18 (about nine units by 2026-11-19); base 0.7.10 is to add a refusal code of its own when a module's DSP claims meet a delay buffer (code 12) and to log which check refused a module at start. The card holds two set slots (MODWERK0.SET, MODWERK1.SET); a set loaded from the card is made the one the next boot prefers while the other stays for recovery. A live CPU/DSP load card on the site (USB). The machine guide now explains the frame guard's budget and how to count skipped renders. New draft Micro Timing 0.1.1-experimental (own_mods); its remembered row moved out of battery RAM into the module's own memory. Zoom MS-70CDR: Sync repairs an effect missing from the pedal's list; the list is written back only while the pedal stays connected. Digitone II: Modwerk's own linker knows OS 1.12 and links core-dn2 0.3 and 0.4 byte for byte as elekloader does, but refuses mods with DSP code; the site builds no Digitone II firmware yet. Base changes now collect in one draft pull request per machine, shipped by the owner after long tests on a unit; device reviewers (assigned per machine) approve first module releases.

### Overwitch

Multitrack Overbridge audio on Linux. Supports Overbridge 2 devices incl. Analog Heat, Heat MKII and Heat +FX, Digitakt I/II, Digitone I/II/Keys, Syntakt. GPL-3.0, 671 commits. 2026-11-18 (README, docs/adding.md on main, no release yet): Overbridge 1 devices (Analog Four MKI, Analog Keys, Analog Rytm MKI) are supported with recent OS versions that speak the Overbridge 2 protocol (e.g. A4 MKI OS 1.56); only the Analog Four MKI is tested. Their track layout is set per device and can be written to the device from the GUI; their blocks hold 1 ms of audio (1-5 blocks, default 3).

_Latest seen (2026-10-31, secondary directories): altstrument: v2.2 (2025-12-21), GPL-3.0-or-later, JACK clients streaming multitrack Overbridge 2 audio._

### Sidecar | Expander

A Raspberry Pi 4B/5 on the Rytm's USB port adds digital voices, effects and a sequencer; the Rytm runs a patched OS. 0.3.2 adds experimental, emulator-only Digitakt support. The Teensy variant is frozen. GPL-2.0. On 2026-11-09, Analog Four MKII support since 0.4.0 (A4 firmware a4-v0.12, OS 1.56); 0.4.3 caps the Rytm screen redraws after users saw a sluggish Rytm at 20-40 redraws a second. 2026-11-13: a card config editor on the documentation site writes the Pi's config.txt and cmdline.txt in the browser. 2026-11-15 (INSTALL-PI): from Sidecar 0.5.0 a release is to ship a starter zip that fills one FAT32 card with the boot files, a new web app (in a hidden folder), every user machine and effect, starter content and demo samples; without the web-app folder the Pi serves the classic page. 2026-11-16 (README, RELEASE-NOTES 0.5.0, KNOWN-ISSUES, docs): 0.5.0 drops the OS 1.73 build; the Pi 5 is now the recommended board (2 GB minimum, 4 GB recommended); MORPH, the looper and sidechain moved to 0.5.1. The 0.5.0 features are marked in testing on their pages. The voices clipped at the stock Rytm's track ceiling in 0.4.x and now play 9 dB lower. Do not combine with newer elekloader cores: they store their settings in the bytes Sidecar uses. 2026-11-18 (README, RELEASE-NOTES 0.5.1, docs): 0.5.1 updates only the Pi, from the web page (a .scu file, a trial boot, automatic return to 0.5.0 if it does not come back). MORPH, the looper, sidechain and a new WAVETABLE moved again, to 0.5.2. A catalog in the web page installs community user machines from a public registry (trigcondition/sidecar-machines): native code, no sandbox, not tested by Sidecar. A USB host that vanished mid-traffic on the Pi's USB-C port halted the Pi in 0.5.0; 0.5.1 recovers.

_Related: mod for `elekloader` (README: the Rytm firmware part is an elekloader module); uses tool `analog-emu` (README: built or checked in trigcondition/analog-emu) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

### Sidecar | Expander: Rytm mods

The source of the Analog Rytm MKII OS mods that Sidecar | Expander needs: patch sources, symbol map, allocation registry and the build that turns the user's own stock .syx into a modded one, as one elekloader module per OS; the Analog Four MKII's mod in a4/. 0.4.0 reports each track's pan and route (stereo through mode), adds MD's own page, preset browsers for JUNO and 6-OP FM, DSP SAMPLE's sample picker, list knobs of up to 36 names, a MIDI machine (machine 50) and arpeggiator settings in the sound. Sidecar Mini (Teensy) is frozen at 0.1.0. 2026-11-16 (v0.5.0): SAMPLER as machine 43, the Rytm's own sound parameters moved from the Pi (an offset or override added in the audio interrupt, never written to the kit), UP + RIGHT for FILL, a browser preview and file menu, send effect BASE/WIDTH. It needs elekloader core 0.1: newer cores keep their settings in the same bytes and the set is refused as an overlap. A mod SysEx report sent between the parts of a stock pattern dump cut the dump; fixed in 0.5.0 (I111).

### elkbench (hardware tests as an MCP server)

One local MCP server per PC that gives AI agent sessions the same tools for testing Elektron units (Analog Rytm MKII, Analog Four MKII, Digitone; Digitakt untested on hardware) and their emulators: claim a unit, run a test plan, flash an OS, take screenshots, record and check USB audio, take or restore an Overbridge Total Recall image. It enforces one owner per unit, emulator first, and a hardware run only after the person says go. Python stdlib; Windows and Linux. 2026-11-10: a flash between two fixed OS files of a unit can reuse an emulator pass of the same flash, recorded with the hashes of the emulator, the flash tool and the card, while all of them stay the same. 2026-11-11 (config example): an optional emulator headroom check waits for CPU, free RAM and a cap on running emulators before each emulator start. 2026-11-12: emulator timing (analog-emu unit or exact timing, the Sidecar's Overbridge stream on the Rytm) and a CPU gate that fails an emulator run at 95 % CPU. 2026-11-13: elklock marks a unit that stalled on its restart after a flash and refuses every device command on it until a watched power cycle (elkflash usb-cycle). 2026-11-14: DIN MIDI interfaces are configured per interface, not per unit; at a run's first DIN step elkbench probes each interface with the unit's working-kit dump request and uses the one that answers, so a cable can move between units without a config change; elklock locks each interface as its own device.

_Related: uses tool `analog-emu` (README: emulator first; sidecar-emu reaches analog-emu through it) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

_Sources: state/NEW.md 2026-11-10, README, README, config.example.toml (2026-11-14)_

### sidecar-emu (Sidecar emulator)

QEMU cut down to the Raspberry Pi 4B and the devices Sidecar's engine needs: boots the Sidecar engine image, answers over Ethernet, puts an Analog Rytm MKII stand-in on its USB-A side and gives its USB-C gadget a raw MIDI TCP port, so an OS upgrade or an elkbench run can go through the emulated Pi into analog-emu. A local experiment, not meant for QEMU upstream. 2026-11-19 (README): a usb-teensy device stands in for the Teensy 4.1 relay of the Sidecar firmware (its link protocol and the HalfKay bootloader, with fault options for flows that failed on the unit), behind an emulated high-speed USB hub, so a Teensy flash through the Pi can be rehearsed in the emulator.

_Related: uses tool `analog-emu` (README: through the emulated Pi into analog-emu); cites `sidecar-expander` (README: emulates the Sidecar engine) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

_Sources: state/NEW.md 2026-11-10, README, README (2026-11-19)_

### trig-seedr

Offline pattern algorithms as an elekloader mod, opened as a third TRIG page after EUCLIDEAN: generate rhythms, notes, accents, trig conditions, retrigs and sample locks for a track, audition takes with undo, apply groove timing and velocity, and rotate a track or the whole pattern. Everything it writes is ordinary pattern data that plays and saves on a stock OS. Analog Four MKII and Syntakt are planned. Groove tables can be made from the user's own Ableton Live grooves; none are shipped. The author names Claude as coding assistant. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-15; README and firmware notes read 2026-11-15. 2026-11-16 (v0.4.0/v0.4.1, README 0.5): navigation is LEFT/RIGHT, PAGE and the TRIG keys stay stock's while the page is open. 0.4.1 is the build to flash: 0.4.0 wrote new trigs without the stock SYN/SMP/ENV flag bits, and a compiler optimisation (store merging in m68k-elf-gcc 16.2) broke a step move in the emulator (I112). Recipes live in RAM only and are lost at power-off or a pattern change. The MAP source copies Grids' drum map (GPL-3.0, Mutable Instruments, not catalogued). 2026-11-17 (v0.5.0-v0.7.0, README, release notes, flashing, testing, firmware notes): first hardware passes on a Rytm MKII (0.5.1, 0.6.0). Since 0.5.1 YES writes a take only with grid recording on and a take stays only after FUNC + YES; changing track or pattern, closing or turning RECORD off restores the original. Fuzzing found that two lock lanes on one parameter lost locks (the Rytm keeps one lock per parameter and step); refused since 0.6.0. The mod is 62 KB of code and 107 KB of RAM. Planned after 1.0: a TURING page that rewrites the track at each loop end. 2026-11-18 (v0.7.1, README, manual, flashing, testing, status M2.6): 0.7 is declared a beta for users; feedback decides what changes before 1.0. 0.7.1 fixes YOLO: take() fell off its end without a return value, so whether a roll stayed depended on a leftover register; the emulator passed by chance (I142). The mod now builds with -Werror=return-type. Boot screen shows T071 (a patch release shows Txyz, a minor one TSxy). 2026-11-20 (README, docs/firmware-notes-st142.md, flashing-st.md, plan-syntakt.md, status S0.2-U3, mods/*-st, manual): a Syntakt OS 1.42 port is in development, tested in analog-emu only (102 emulator checks), with no file offered to flash; the beta stays Rytm-only, so `devices` stays analog-rytm. The mod's code is split into a device-neutral frame/ and one part per device. On the Syntakt it uses a minimal hook-bus core of its own (456 bytes, from Synfact's GPL sources) because Synfact's core-st 2.0.3 does not link with gcc 16.2, so it does not run beside Synfact's mods. Code and data sit at 0x47a00000-0x47b00000, a range the emulator never saw the OS use; a canary mod is to check that on a unit with all 64 sample slots loaded. Differences from the Rytm: no retrigs, accent or slide; NOTE only (chord notes kept); LOCK lists the track's machine's controls; no lock-row limit. The unit file is stock 1.42 rebuilt by elektron-firmware-tool with only MAIN changed. A device header (st_params.h) is generated from the user's own stock file and never committed. Unit steps planned: practise the startup-menu recovery, flash a round-tripped stock file, the canary, then the mod. Rytm manual: YES + SCENE does not save a pattern while the mod is open (the mod takes YES, SCENE closes it).

### LEDrum (Sidecar drum voice)

A drum voice for the Sidecar expander (a Raspberry Pi beside the Analog Rytm MKII) as a Pi user machine (.rmp): a modified port of the open-source Erica Synths LXR-02 drum voice, rewritten for float processing at 48 kHz with new envelopes and filter; the LXR wavetables and transient samples are used unchanged. Listed in the Sidecar community machine registry. Native code with no sandbox. Not affiliated with Erica Synths or Elektron. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-18.

_Related: mod for `sidecar-expander` (README: a user machine for Sidecar, installed into /Plugins on its SD card) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

### Sidecar community machine registry

The registry of community user machines and effects for the Sidecar expander (.rmp packages built for the Pi 4, Pi 5 or Teensy), from which Sidecar's web catalogue installs them. Each package comes with a manifest (id, version, board, plugin API, SHA-256, licence) and a README; tools/check.py validates a submission without loading it (header magic, format, API, board, sizes, CRC-32, relocations) and refuses changes to published files. The packages are native code with no sandbox. Most are by trigcondition, several by amnmkkr (LEDrum among them). Was a candidate (2026-11-18); read 2026-11-19. 2026-11-20 (README, CONTRIBUTING.md, docs/index-format.md): a version may carry 1-8 MP3 audio previews (at most 2 MB each, 10 MB a version) for the catalogue page; the checker validates their names and MP3 frame chain without decoding; previews are not covered by the package's SHA-256. No new packages.

_Related: mod for `sidecar-expander` (README: packages for Sidecar; Sidecar 0.5.1 installs them from its web catalogue) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_
